page: Microsoft Azure EC64as_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by AMD x86_64 processors and managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The configuration provides 64 dedicated vCPUs coupled with 512.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an 8.0 GB memory-to-core ratio. The instance does not include integrated hardware acceleration, operating with zero GPUs.

Storage architecture on the EC64as_v6 relies entirely on remote disk attachments, as the instance features no bundled local disk capacity. It is designed to interface directly with Azure Premium Storage to deliver persistent input and output throughput. Network connectivity does not bundle complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating configured private networking or provisioned external addressing.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high RAM allocation per core positions the EC64as_v6 effectively for enterprise footprints requiring dense in-memory capacity without requiring disproportionate compute over-provisioning. The absence of local temporary drives eliminates the overhead of managing ephemeral storage while ensuring data persistence is managed centrally on durable block storage.

The EC64as_v6 is suited for memory-intensive workloads that demand substantial continuous RAM capacity, such as large-scale in-memory relational and non-relational databases, distributed caching layers, enterprise resource planning applications, and heavy in-memory data analytics pipelines.
